    "title": "Dowling geometry Kinser-inequality conjecture",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let a **Dowling geometry** be the matroid constructed from the corresponding labelled graph whose circuits are the positive cycles and minimal connected subgraphs containing two negative cycles.     "title": "Regularity conjecture for weakly closed graphs",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be a connected weakly closed graph, let $S=K[x_1,\\ldots,x_n,y_1,\\ldots,y_n]$, and let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal.     "title": "Lescure–Meyniel conjecture for strong immersions",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be a graph, let $chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $K_{chi(G)}$ be the complete graph on $chi(G)$ vertices. A **strong immersion** of a graph $H$ in $G$ consists of an injection from $V(H)$ to $V(G)$ and pairwise edge-disjoint paths representing the edges of $H$, whose internal vertices avoid the image of the injection. **Lescure–Meyniel conjecture.** Every graph $G$ contains a strong immersion of $K_{chi(G)}$. This is the strong-immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture. It implies the Abu-Khzam–Langston conjecture for weak immersions, and both conjectures remain open in general; the statement is known for chromatic number at most $7$.",

    "literal_statement": "Let $C$ be a finite or countable graph with no isolated vertices.
